findings.text: _store_history_rows treats a store with no rows for the project as an answer and never falls through to the committed ledger — run_store.stored_run_rows returns an empty list when the store file exists (reckon/run_store.py:1028-1030, docstring 1011-1012) while reckon/ledger.py:2861-2864 falls through on any empty answer — so held_section_blockers at reckon/roadmap.py:3812 reports a ledger-only project's delivered nodes as free and the queue can re-dispatch them.

the added read duplicates the capability reckon/ledger.py:_load_file_history already owns (store-then-ledger selection, plan narrowing through stored_run_rows(plan=...), picker projection); it neither extends nor wraps that owner, which is how the fallback divergence above arose.

the index keeps a node's last row by iteration order, but stored_run_rows yields main rows before archived rows (reckon/run_store.py:785-799, ORDER BY rowid), so a node re-promoted after its earlier row was retired keeps the older archived run_id and completed_at; the hold itself is unaffected.

rubric.evidence claims the brief-carried plan fallback is asserted by the queue-ordering test, but no gate log runs tests/test_queue_ordering_reads_history_once.py or tests/test_a_brief_carried_run_counts_toward_its_section.py, the two files covering held_section_blockers and that fallback.

two of the five declared write paths — the evidence fragment and its figure directory under docs/evidence/fragments/the-fleet-node-stays-inside-its-memory/ — carry no change, so the section's measured result is recorded only in the run manifest and not on the plan page.

item_verdicts.diff: read commit by commit from ebad3fef to ee7298959c: d2b9899943 reads a node's hold from its own store rows and ee7298959c keeps the hold index rather than the decoded rows, +328/-49 over two files.
item_verdicts.done_when: the four-arm profile was run and logged (measure.log, measure2.log, doubled-{base,head}.log) and the unmet ratios are recorded in manifest.md:15 beside the base-revision negative control that fails in negative-control-base-tests.log.
item_verdicts.goal: §8's deliverable asks that a batch dispatch hold one node's delivered-run records at a time so its peak no longer scales with the store; reckon/crew/section_holds.py:357 narrows held_node_rows to one node, but the delivered doubling arm shows the head's forty-entry peak still rising 89 % when the store doubles, contradicting the goal's second clause.
item_verdicts.manifest: read; reports complete at ee7298959c with 60 passed at the head and 58 at the base, the gate command and log paths, and the unmet criterion stated in the landing line.
item_verdicts.write_paths: five declared; the diff touches only reckon/crew/section_holds.py and tests/test_dispatch_batch_memory_profile.py, both inside the declared set, with the declared fragment and figure undelivered.

justifications.durability: the two added assertions redden against the replaced read (negative-control-base-tests.log records 603 and 600 rows decoded and 2 failed), but no test covers the store-to-committed-ledger fallback the change removes.
justifications.evidence: the gate is the done_when's own profile and its logs exist (after_suite-1795333166697187097.log EXIT=0, negative-control-base-tests.log EXIT=1), though the head and base figures in the landing line come from different jobs.
justifications.fit: the added names describe the mechanism and the local-import and noqa: BLE001 idioms match the module's existing style at reckon/crew/section_holds.py:77.
justifications.goal_fidelity: reckon/crew/section_holds.py:190 bounds the hold answer to one node's rows, while the delivered doubling arm recorded in manifest.md:15 shows the peak still scaling with the store.
justifications.reuse: _store_history_rows at reckon/crew/section_holds.py:163 re-implements the capability reckon/ledger.py:2844 _load_file_history owns and drops its empty-store fallthrough.
justifications.scope_discipline: both changed files lie inside the declared write paths and nothing outside them is touched, with the declared fragment and figure left undelivered.
